headline: Profit surges on acquisitions; margins compress
summary_short: Celsius Holdings' Q1 2026 revenue was $782.6M (+137.7% y/y, +8.5% q/q) on the Alani Nu and Rockstar acquisitions, with net income of $110.1M and diluted EPS of $0.33, though gross margin fell to 48.3% from 52.3% a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue nearly tripled y/y to $782.6M as North America grew $440.8M, driven by Alani Nu (+$368.1M) and Rockstar (+$66.6M); Europe grew 35.9%. Gross margin fell 400bp to 48.3% on higher promotional spend, aluminum costs, and integration-related freight/tariff pressure. SG&A rose 95% to $234.6M on the three-brand portfolio buildout and a $25.5M litigation charge. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $85.1M ($0.33 diluted EPS), helped by revenue growth but offset by Series B preferred dividends and $11.8M higher interest expense on acquisition debt. Operating cash flow fell $29.7M y/y to $73.7M on distributor-termination settlements. Cash was $549.2M; the company repurchased $24.1M of stock and paid $7.2M in Series B preferred dividends. No forward guidance was stated in the filing.

drivers.explanation: Results reflect the first full quarter operating as a three-brand portfolio (Celsius, Alani Nu, Rockstar) under the expanded Pepsi distribution partnership following the 2025 Rockstar Acquisition and Series B Preferred Stock issuance.

North America revenue +$440.8M was driven primarily by the Alani Nu Acquisition (+$368.1M) and the Rockstar Acquisition (+$66.6M); Europe grew 35.9% to $25.4M on new market launches and distribution investment.
Margin fell to 48.3% from 52.3% on increased promotional activity as a % of revenue and higher aluminum costs; freight costs also rose on integration disruptions, freeze protection, and tariffs.
Not separately narrated; the increase is explained by gross profit growth (+$205.7M) outpacing SG&A growth (+$114.3M) and a modest $4.4M distributor termination charge.
Not discussed separately in the release; tracks the operating-income increase since depreciation/amortization was not reported as materially different q/q or y/y.

Driven by revenue and gross-profit growth from the Alani Nu and Rockstar acquisitions, partially offset by Series B preferred dividends, higher acquisition-related interest expense, and higher SG&A from the three-brand expansion.
